title: psoralea imbricata
intro: Psoralea imbricata, commonly known as Bishop's Weed, is a plant species in the legume family. It has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, which may help to treat conditions such as eczema, arthritis, and wounds. The therapeutic actions of Bishop's Weed include its ability to modulate the immune system, reduce inflammation, and exhibit hepatoprotective properties. The bioactive constituents of Psoralea imbricata include coumarins, lignans, and alkaloids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
